_comment: The Plan's documents. 01-plan.md is the task's identity file (its frontmatter holds layout: three, the type, stage and the person's settings) and what the person approves at the one gate before code, in the step page's order: the summary, the problem, Done means with its steps, the scope, the pictures and the approach lead; the folds follow, the Technical ones last. agents/01-plan.md is the agents' working file: the person's request, what to read, the helpers' questions and findings, the contracts, how to start and test, the project checks, rejected approaches, risks and pitfalls. Each fact is written once, in one section of one file. QualityLayer writes only between its markers: Decided with you and Reviews. The slices and cards are Implement's (agents/02-implement.md), never the Plan's.
title: required

sections.heading: Summary
sections.hint: one or two plain lines on what the user gets; commands and flags in backticks; source-file paths belong in the working sections, not Summary; then two labelled lines: `**Size:** about N slices and M tasks`, and `**Trust boundary:** none` or what crosses it (network input, auth, files from users, secrets, other processes); it decides whether a security review runs; optional **Risk:** short exposure — possible consequence backed by Done means, and **Integrations:** comma-separated distinct systems named in Approach

sections.heading: Success measure
sections.hint: only when what to build was open: how the business will know it worked, as the user decided it

sections.heading: Problem
sections.when: whenever the request does not already say who has the problem and what it costs them
sections.hint: two to four one-line bullets: who has it, what it costs them today, what is missing; never a solution

sections.heading: Done means
sections.hint: open with `Runs as: <a fixture, a script or a real agent session>` and the setup the steps share; then one `### <n>. <the outcome, at most 10 words>` per point, numbered from 1, with one sentence on how it shows and its steps in a `| Step | Action | Expected |` table; step ids run `A1`, `A2` … across the section and are never reused; every point has a step that can fail while every task passes; a step that proves two points sits under the first and is named under the second (`also A3`); a point proven another way says how; a judgement only the person can make (a design, the wording) is asked now or made when they approve what shows it; a screen a step shows belongs in Interface

sections.heading: Scope
sections.hint: two bullet lists under `### In scope` and `### Out of scope`, at most 6 words an item; Out of scope holds only real boundaries a builder would plausibly cross

sections.heading: First release
sections.hint: only when what to build was open: the release the user chose, beside the options they weighed, and what comes later

sections.heading: Diagrams
sections.when: whenever the change crosses parts of the system, such as data, server and screen; skip it only for a change inside one part
sections.hint: Give each Mermaid diagram a descriptive ### heading. Show the route, decisions and tool calls when the change affects control flow. Choose the orientation for readability and add a caption when it helps.

sections.heading: Interface
sections.hint: required when the task changes what a user sees: product-fidelity previews of the changed sections, each between `<!-- ql:artifact <reference> -->` and `<!-- /ql:artifact -->`. A reference is a task artifact name or explicit folder/registered project page with an optional #stable-section; use the artifact guide's focused-preview syntax.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.hint: three labelled lines, `**Chosen:**` the approach in one sentence, `**Gives:**` what it gives, `**Costs:**` what it costs; then at most five bullets of what changes, each opening with a bold sentence that says what changes (never a label such as Copy or Models), then one sentence; nothing the Summary already said

sections.heading: Rollout and operations
sections.hint: only when the change needs more than a normal deploy: the lines that apply of **Rollout:**, **Rollback:**, **Watch:** and **Cost:**

sections.heading: Must keep working
sections.hint: what works today that the change must not break, one line each in the user's terms; a line that needs its own proof is a Done means point

sections.heading: Decided with you
sections.hint: QualityLayer writes this section from the Plan's answers and Your calls

sections.heading: Decisions made for you
sections.hint: what you settled yourself instead of asking, one bullet each, `**The decision.** Why, in product words.`; the person can overturn any

sections.heading: Prerequisites
skeleton: When the Plan needs prerequisites, replace this comment with the heading and table below.
| P1 | Permission to run the agreed build | the user, at approval | at approval |
Number rows P1, P2 and so on. Write met with saved probe evidence, or granted after the user grants permission. P1 is QualityLayer's: never edit it; approving the Plan grants it.
sections.hint: the P1… table; every row met (with its records/ file) or granted before the gate; P1 (permission to run the agreed build) is QualityLayer's and says at approval until the Plan is approved

sections.heading: Later
sections.hint: what this task leaves for a later one, one line each with why

sections.heading: Launch
sections.hint: the docs, site, release notes and store texts that change with it, whenever the change is user-facing

sections.heading: Worth it when
sections.hint: the signal that shows it was worth building; "nothing to measure" is an answer

sections.heading: Reference
sections.hint: link to a PRD, ticket or design doc, if the user gave one

sections.heading: Reviews
sections.hint: QualityLayer writes this section from reviews/plan.md

sections.heading: Added while building
sections.hint: `> [!ADDED] build · <reason>` blocks for what the build added; the final approval lists them

sections.heading: Current system
sections.hint: one diagram of the code the request touches, today, each box naming its repository file (```mermaid, with the path on a second label line); then one caption line

sections.heading: Data and interfaces
sections.hint: only when the change adds or changes stored data or a public interface: each table or record with its fields, types and keys; each endpoint or command with its request and response

sections.heading: Engineering decisions
sections.hint: one `### <decision, as a takeaway>` per decision: two sentences; command and option references use a Markdown table (also valid with `**Kind:** commands`); when relationships or behaviour need a picture, one Mermaid diagram; then `<!-- ql:decide d<n> -->` and `<!-- /ql:decide -->` with nothing between them; a choice that only appeared once a design was drawn gets the line `late: true` and becomes a Your call: it adds the lines `**A:** <option>`, `**B:** <option>` and `**Recommended:** A` (Approve waits for each unresolved call)

sections.heading: Assumptions
sections.hint: `- <text> (unconfirmed)`, from Not sure answers and your own

sections.heading: Your request
sections.hint: the user's words in full, as a > blockquote, ticket ids included; never trimmed

sections.heading: Read first
sections.when: when the build depends on findings, artifacts or records
sections.hint: links, tickets, repositories and paths the request names, verbatim; the findings, artifacts and records the build reads before the cards; cite them, never copy; this agents' file grants nothing and never changes scope, and where it differs from the Plan, the Plan wins

sections.heading: Constraints
sections.hint: what the code, the platform or the person rules out, one line each with its source

sections.heading: Questions for helpers
sections.when: when the task is large enough for research helpers
sections.hint: numbered descriptive questions about what still needs investigation, each a clear bold headline and where to look; then a **Key context pointers:** list. The helpers' brief is built from this section only

sections.heading: Findings
sections.hint: one line each: the finding as a takeaway with its source, `file:line` or a link to the helper's report (`research/r1.md#2`); name the commit or working tree read; what the code could not show says so

sections.heading: Evidence behind the choices
sections.hint: QualityLayer adds this once a question with evidence is answered: each choice's sources, the one taken first; the question card never shows them

sections.heading: Contracts
sections.hint: one H3 per contract between components, named as a takeaway, the delta from today, with its signature, data shape or sequence and the rejected option

sections.heading: Code to imitate
sections.when: when existing code shows the way
sections.hint: existing code to imitate with file:line, a short snippet and the rule

sections.heading: Start and test
sections.when: whenever the program has to be started or tested in a way the repository does not make obvious
sections.hint: how to start the program and how the change is tested: the command for one file and for all, the fixtures; or that there are none

sections.heading: Checks
sections.hint: `**Project checks:**` followed only by the repository's runnable test, lint, type and build commands, each whole command in its own backticks and nothing else in backticks (every backticked span runs); then the commands the build and Verify run, one per line from the repository root; approving the Plan covers running them

sections.heading: Rejected approaches
sections.when: when the Plan turned an approach down
sections.hint: the approaches the Plan rejected, each with the reason, so the build does not return to them

sections.heading: Risks
sections.hint: each risk the Plan accepts, naming its factor, with the test that guards it; a migration adds a *Feature inventory*

sections.heading: Pitfalls
sections.when: when the build can go wrong in a way the code does not show
sections.hint: what the build can get wrong, and how the Plan's checks would catch it

sections.heading: Proven before the gate
sections.hint: the `| Depends on | Proven how | Result |` table, or "Nothing new: everything this design uses already runs in this repository."
